dialogues.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
dialogues.text: Good champion, please, rest your wandering feet here for a spell...

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: It is just as you see, valiant warrior. I and my brothers-in-arms defend this place, just as we have every day for millennia.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A legion? You've got help, then?

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: In the past, yes, but they have departed.

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: Or perhaps they laid down their obsessions and hatreds over the winding years. Perhaps, they were even consumed by said passions, casting duty aside and embracing senseless slaughter.

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: Only I still stand guard here.

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: Noble warrior, come you from the capital? Could you bring word to the citizens there that Legio VI has done their duty — that not a single vishap has passed our leaguer?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are there still vishaps in here?

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: Nay, not for many years now... But the history of our battle has been recorded in the "Symphony" somehow, playing over and over like an opera...

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: I, too, cannot discern truth from illusion. Do you wish to enter and see? A champion from the capital will see no danger there, so please, inscribe our history using your hands and eyes.

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: Caesareum Palace was what we named it once, but today, naught is left but wrack and ruin.

response.speaker: Nameless Stone Statue
response.text: I and fellow legionnaires of Legion Athanatoi defend it still, as we have for thousands of years.
